title: Lucid Minute: runtime journal + micro-tasks
content:
Quick orientation (why this exists):
This is a tight, readable diary for the week of small experiments and triage tickets. Not an RFC — quick captures only. Use bullets liberally. Delete when done.

2025-11-04 — Morning wakeup
08:15 — coffee, skim alerts: brief P99 spike on prod-gpu-4 around 01:30 UTC; related to long-sequence chat jobs.
08:25 — triage notes:
- Incident JIRA-RT-1824: p99+ CPU time increase on the batch_coordinator thread. Symptoms: batch latency jumps, NVLink idle.
- Quick hypothesis: scheduler mis-estimating batch size for long-seq requests => KV cache churn causing extra GPU work.
- Impact: 7% of requests in the window saw tail latency > 800ms, majority on model-xl-8q.

Immediate micro-actions (today):
- [ ] Reproduce locally with simulated long-seq load (script below). Target: hit the same thread stack traces.
- [ ] Add lightweight logging in batch_coordinator: capture batch_size distribution and kv_cache_evictions per epoch. Short-term, log at trace-level so ops can toggle.
- [ ] Validate our model-variant fallback path triggers properly when queue length > X.
- [ ] Postmortem stub: capture timeline and attach perf flame on JIRA-RT-1824.

Quick repro script (run on my laptop / a dev-GPU):
# run-sim-longseq.sh (very rough)
# python load_generator.py --model model-xl-8q --seq 4096 --qps 6 --duration 300

Notes-to-self about debugging stacktraces:
- Check for: batch_coordinator -> scheduler::choose_batch -> kv_cache::recompute when seq_len > 2048.
- If stack shows nvtx markers but low GPU util, suspect prefix cache thrash.

Observations from a 10m smoke test at 09:10:
- With simulated sequences of 3k tokens at 2 qps across 8 workers, I saw steady latency except occasional spikes when batch sizes jumped above 16.
- Adding a coarse backpressure gate at queue length 128 eliminated the spikes in the smoke run (works as a mitigation).

Short-term mitigations (candidate list):
- Implement soft cap on batch_size for long sequences (prefer smaller, faster batches).
- Add a temporary routing rule: long-seq requests route to a high-memory but lower-concurrency pool (if available).
- Backpressure threshold at queue_length 128 with early 429 to caller (documented in API notes).

Midday pairing plan:
- 11:00 with Arun: instrumented logs and light metrics (batch_size histogram + kv_evictions) — goal to push a test branch by EOD.
- 14:30 with Mina: discuss failover policy for model-xl-8q when under high long-seq load.

Loose ideas to evaluate (not today):
- Explore a prefix-aware scheduler that favors pinned KV caches for sequences that likely reuse prefixes (heuristic: same conversation id).
- Consider a micro-cache per-worker for very recent KV entries to reduce cross-worker cache misses during bursts. Cost: memory + bookkeeping.

Open questions / To research:
- Is the model-variant fallback aggressive enough? (Can we shift policy to fallback earlier?)
- Does quantized variant produce the same output quality for these long-seq workloads? Need to run eval set.
- How often do conversational clients send repeated prefix tokens vs unique? (affects cache hit rate)

Personal TODO (short list):
- [ ] push logging PR: runtime: batch-coordinator quick-trace (ref PR 724) — assign to Arun for review.
- [ ] run the smoky load for 30m on dev cluster and capture flame graphs.
- [ ] write short note for ops with mitigation steps and 429 guidance.
- [ ] save experiment artifacts to /tmp/lucia/longseq-exps and share link in JIRA.

Triage checklist (when handling similar incidents):
1) Collect stack traces + nvprof timeline.
2) Check batch_size distribution + queued requests histogram.
3) Check kv_cache eviction rate per worker.
4) Try emergency soft-cap and observe effect.
5) Decide whether to route long-seq to fallback pool.

Evening quick reflection (11/04):
- Ran 30m smoke: the backpressure gate reduced spikes but increased rejected requests ~0.8% (acceptable for now).
- Logging PR prepared, tests added for batch-size histogram.
- Next day focus: evaluate fallback routing and run eval for quantized variant.

Random mental notes (delete later):
- Could we add a small SLA-based hint header so callers can mark "latency-sensitive" vs "throughput-sensitive"? That would help scheduler heuristics.
- Check with Product if 429 semantics acceptable (they might prefer queueing and retries client-side).

End of entry.

---
If this doc persists, convert to a short postmortem and copy mitigation steps to service-runbook (ops).
